video_title: Jalen Brunson Breaks Down How the Knicks ATTACKED Wemby

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins explains the origin of Jalen Brunson's nickname
quotes.excerpt: you got to understand how you earned the name Big Body Brunson
quotes.quote: You got to understand how you earned the name Big Body Brunson, bro. You 6'1, 6'2. We are not counting the shoes and the orthotics and tape, bro. But you play like you are a seven-footer, and when I say that is because offensively, you do not shy away from physicality. You embrace physicality. You have a post game, you are always being guarded by people that are bigger than you and you always find a way. You will take them to the low block, finishing in traffic, giving them the shoulder, getting separation. I had to break it down to you why you got that nickname.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the Knicks' offensive shift under Mike Brown
quotes.excerpt: I felt like this year something changed with Mike Brown. Was that true?
quotes.quote: I honestly did not think a smaller guard would win the way that usually smaller guards are played last year, year before that. But I felt like this year something changed with Mike Brown. Was that true? Or was it like how was that buying into a new system? Like Jalen Brunson had more assists this year, OG Anunoby I think had more assists, Josh Hart had more assists. What was that like switching it up?

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on the Knicks' collective buy-in during the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: everyone always says the right thing, right? And then we get to the point where we are down 2-1.
quotes.quote: Everyone always says the right thing, right? And then we get to the point where we are down 2-1. We have done a lot of good things up to this point, and we have had some ups and downs obviously. What was it, we were 2-9 at one point, but the majority of the year we were playing well. So we get to this point where we are down 2-1 and it was like, all right, do we do the things we say we are going to do? Do we do everything it takes to win, or do we just like fold? So like, you know, we kind of all after that game, just reassessed everything that needed to be done and we just went back to work.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson calls the Knicks' playoff run the greatest he has seen
quotes.excerpt: I personally think it is the greatest championship run that I have seen.
quotes.quote: I personally think it is the greatest championship run that I have seen, right? Like what you guys did, kind of being down 2-1 to wheeling off, what was it, 13 in a row? So down 2-1 to the Hawks, who that is Channing's favorite fan base, to 13-0. And then I, in my opinion, just the way you guys handled the finals, I have never witnessed a run like that before, especially given, you know, the amount of championship experience that you guys had on your team, a brand new head coach, what you guys did in the finals, the comebacks over the course.

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson identifies the most surprising moment of the Knicks' playoff run
quotes.excerpt: the easy answer would be the finals one, Game 4 with OG.
quotes.quote: The easy answer would be the finals one, Game 4 with OG. Just being down what, 29? But I think we were down 29 with a lot of time left. The one that is like crazy was like we were down, what was it, 22 in the fourth to the Cavs. So now that, that is the one, with like seven minutes left and then all of a sudden we just go on this, we just, we just go on this run and then we are here. But like, yeah, Game 4 of the finals I think obviously was like the the craziest one, but I think the most surprising is Game 1 of the conference finals.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on the Knicks' defensive strategy against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: you were basically picking on the defensive player of the year.
quotes.quote: In that second half and that fourth quarter, y'all did something. You started to do, you did something that no one expected to be done. Like the comeback was one thing, but y'all were basically picking on the defensive player of the year. Like if I could recall, y'all, no seriously bro, y'all put him like, I think he was involved in like 21 of the actions in the fourth quarter. Like there's times you could go see the the video circulating of y'all putting him in action. Like, no, we want you, like you was bringing him up in the pick and roll. Like was that the game plan or was y'all just on some like, no, we just, this is what it is, we go wear you down, make you play defense, make you slide these puppies on the perimeter?

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on the necessity of targeting Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: you have to be aware of where he is at all times.
quotes.quote: Playing against him, it is like you have to be aware of where he is at all times, right? All right. And so when he is on the help side, which is primarily what they want to do, right? Put him on the help side and he is able to alter shots or not even like you you think about shooting once you drive the back like drive to the basket, everyone kind of like rotates around him. So being able to put him in the action, if we get around him, then all of a sudden they are in rotation and we are able to be the team we want to be. But just like kind of trying to find ways to put them in positions where they weren't as comfortable.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Jalen Brunson's role as the Knicks' primary playmaker
quotes.excerpt: you are the man with the ball and like it is wild watching you at the end.
quotes.quote: You ran a lot of action that seemed like where Cat had the ball, right, this year, especially I think in the finals. And what was that like trusting him? Like you are the man with the ball and like it is wild watching you at the end of game make the right play after the right play after the right play. What is it like in your mind being like, here Cat, the right play is for you to have it, and then me to set that like almost impossible down screen for OG and then that little curl and doing actions like that? So adding that into your repertoire of like things that are are like a part of the Knicks and success, what was that like in your mind?

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on the Knicks' offensive rhythm and decision-making
quotes.excerpt: Cat, he was making the right decisions 90% of the time.
quotes.quote: It was obviously helpful, but it was it took I don't want to say it took an adjustment period. I think once we kind of started to do it, it seemed kind of natural because, you know, Cat, he was making the right decisions 90% of the time. Like he was making even if like it was if we turn the ball over, it was an aggressive pass. It was aggressive. It wasn't like passive stuff. So things that we can live with. For him to kind of make the right decisions and then all of a sudden be in attack at the same time, like it was something that you had to guard and it was something that people haven't seen.
